BiblicalUsage: Melek is the Aramaic word for king, and it runs through Daniel and Ezra as the title of the rulers who held God's people. Daniel 2:4 has the Chaldeans answer the king in Syriack, O king, live for ever, and Daniel 2:37 calls Nebuchadnezzar a king of kings, given kingdom and power and strength and glory by the God of heaven. Daniel 7:17 turns the word to prophecy, where four great beasts are four kings, and Ezra 7:12 shows Artaxerxes, king of kings, writing to Ezra the priest.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the Aramaic chapters of Daniel make one point plain: kings rise and fall by God's hand, and the king of kings answers to the God of heaven. My position is that no throne is final except His, and every king in Daniel proves it, whether he bows or is broken.
